_program.title: 1-Week Interview Readiness Training Plan
_program.subtitle: Final Draft - 5 Training Days | 16 Mandatory Deliverables
_program.purpose: This document converts the old 10-day training structure into a compressed 1-week plan while retaining the required day-wise deliverables, evaluation gates, recording standards, and trainer/candidate responsibilities.

key_updated_rules.rule: All five project scenarios are mandatory Day 2 deliverables. The old plan already required one video per scenario, and the new plan preserves this requirement.
Trainers will prepare PPT-style explanation documents for live explanation. These are trainer-led teaching materials, not separately counted as deliverables.
After the live explanation, trainers provide the project scenario documents to candidates. Candidates prepare from those documents and create the five project scenario video deliverables.
The trainer provides a 60-question resume-based question document. This is source material for preparation and is not counted separately in the 16 deliverables.
Candidates submit one 15-question Resume-Based PUD deliverable on Day 3 and one 15-question Resume-Based PUD deliverable on Day 4.

quality_auto_fail_standards.requirement: Candidate should not read answers or use visible prompts during video deliverables.
Deliverables should be continuous where video is required. Edited/stitched recordings should be rejected unless trainer approves due to technical issue.
Candidate must clearly define what they owned, influenced, and did not own. Over-claiming is a risk condition.
Audio and video must be clear enough for evaluation. Poor quality requires re-recording.
Deliverables should be submitted before the next training day unless trainer gives an exception.
Trainer can mark status as Pass, Partial, or Hold based on submission quality and readiness.

sections.name: Prerequisite and Readiness Validation
sections.detail: Trainer verifies the candidate's complete environment, tooling, documents, and recording readiness before any teaching begins, and resolves any missing access on the spot rather than continuing with an unready setup. Confirm connectivity and hardware: a stable internet connection with no background downloads, updates, or streaming, and a LAN cable connected (this is mandatory — training should not begin on Wi-Fi alone). Confirm the session tools: Getscreen installed and signed in with the required account, the Zoom desktop app installed and logged in, the shared Google Doc opening correctly in the browser (with the phone app as a backup), a microphone tested for clear audio, and adequate camera and lighting. Confirm the machine is distraction-free: Bluetooth off, laptop notifications disabled, all unnecessary apps closed, and the laptop plugged into the charger. Confirm the development setup: Python installed and verified with a basic command-line test, VS Code or another local IDE with a working Python environment ready (online compilers should be avoided), an active GitHub account with at least one academic or personal project, and Docker/Node.js where relevant to the profile (especially frontend or full-stack). Confirm the assigned pre-watch preparation video was completed before the batch started.

sections.name: Program Orientation
sections.detail: Trainer walks the candidate through the full 1-week plan so expectations are unambiguous from the start. Explain the five-day structure and the sixteen mandatory deliverables, the per-day deliverable counts, the submission deadlines (each day's outputs are due before the next training day), the quality gates (each deliverable is marked Pass, Partial, or Hold), and the concrete consequences of missing or failing deliverables. Set the week-long quality and auto-fail standards up front: no reading or visible prompts during video deliverables, no edited or stitched takes (continuous recording required unless the trainer approves an exception for a technical issue), ownership honesty (the candidate must clearly state what they owned, influenced, and did not own — over-claiming is a risk condition), clear audio/video quality, and timely submission. Make sure the candidate understands how the plan and the exit gates work before any content is taught.
key_points: Explain the 1-week / 5-day structure and 16 mandatory deliverables
Explain per-day deliverable counts and submission deadlines (before next day)
Explain quality gates: Pass / Partial / Hold
Explain consequences of missing or failing deliverables
Set auto-fail standards: no reading/prompts, no edited takes

sections.name: Interview Foundations
sections.detail: Trainer demonstrates and coaches the delivery mechanics that underpin every interview answer, then has the candidate practice them. Cover professional posture, steady eye contact, and clean answer framing; the use of deliberate pauses instead of fillers; appropriate tone; respecting time limits; and a disciplined method for handling questions the candidate does not know (acknowledge, reason aloud, avoid bluffing). Reinforce the overall delivery-and-confidence goals: calm tone, eye contact, upright posture, controlled pauses, correct timing, and stopping cleanly rather than rambling. Have the candidate practice one or two short answers applying correct posture, framing, pauses, and a clean stop.
key_points: Demonstrate posture, eye contact, and answer framing
Coach deliberate pauses (no fillers) and appropriate tone
Enforce time limits per answer
Teach handling unknowns without bluffing
Reinforce delivery: tone, eye contact, posture, pauses, timing, stopping discipline
Candidate practices 1-2 short answers with correct delivery
sections.candidate_focus: Practice 1-2 short answers with correct delivery.

sections.name: HR Questions
sections.detail: Trainer teaches how HR/behavioral questions are actually evaluated and coaches a repeatable answer structure. Explain the intent behind common HR questions (what the interviewer is really probing for), the required answer structure of a direct answer followed by a brief explanation and then a clean stop, the common variations of each question, the red flags interviewers watch for, and the common mistakes candidates make (rambling, over-explaining, no clear answer, negativity). Have the candidate practice selected HR answers aloud using the direct-answer / brief-explanation / clean-stop structure with correct timing.

Teach answer structure: direct answer -> brief explanation -> clean stop

sections.detail: Trainer establishes clarity on the candidate's niche/core technical concepts and models the interview-style way to explain them. Explain the key niche concepts relevant to the candidate's profile with practical, concrete examples, and demonstrate the interview-style explanation flow: state the concept simply, give a real example, and keep the explanation to a focused two-to-three-minute flow. Emphasize concept correctness with simple language over jargon. Have the candidate attempt niche answers aloud and clarify any doubts as they arise.

Then brief the two Day 1 deliverables and the recording rules: the HR Questions Recording (recommended 10-15 minutes) and the Niche Fundamentals Recording (recommended 15-20 minutes), each as a single continuous recording, with no notes or prompts, no retakes unless the trainer asks for a re-record due to an audio/video issue, and submission before Day 2. 2.title: Project Scenario Defense, PUD Understanding and Career Flow
2.day_objective: Train the candidate to explain all five project scenarios, understand the Project Understanding Document, and deliver a strong introduction and career flow.

focus_areas.objective: Prepare all five mandatory project scenarios as video deliverables.
Convert project experience into Situation, Task, Action, Result format.
Explain how the project should be understood, structured, and defended.
Train the candidate to explain ownership, decisions, failures, and measurable impact.
Prepare a polished intro and career story for interviews.

special_rules.rule: Trainers create project scenario documents in PPT-style explanation format for live session explanation.
After live explanation, trainers provide the documents to candidates for preparation.
Candidates prepare from the provided documents and record one video for each project scenario.
The PPT-style documents are training material. The five candidate videos are counted as deliverables.

Why a technical choice was made, alternatives considered, and trade-offs accepted.
How a production/system issue was detected, handled, recovered, and prevented.
How one request moves through the system from user/client to backend, processing, data, response, logs, and monitoring.

sections.name: Project Interview Foundation
sections.detail: Trainer explains how project-based interviews are actually judged so the candidate understands the bar before preparing scenarios. Cover the dimensions interviewers score: depth of understanding, personal ownership, use of the STAR structure (Situation, Task, Action, Result), measurable metrics and impact, honest handling of failures, and the ability to withstand follow-up probing. Set the expectation that every project answer should demonstrate genuine ownership and quantifiable impact rather than vague team-level description.

Personal ownership
STAR structure (Situation, Task, Action, Result)

sections.name: Project Scenario Explanation - All Five
sections.detail: Trainer explains all five mandatory project scenarios live using the PPT-style scenario documents, covering for each one its intent, structure, worked examples, the rejection triggers that would fail it, and the must-include points. The five scenarios are: (1) Failure and Learning Story - what failed, why it failed, how it was corrected, and what was learned; (2) Design Trade-Off / Decision Story - why a technical choice was made, what alternatives were considered, and which trade-offs were accepted; (3) System Failure and Recovery Story - how a production/system issue was detected, handled, recovered, and prevented from recurring; (4) End-to-End Request Flow - how a single request moves through the system from user/client to backend, processing, data, response, logs, and monitoring; and (5) Security / Compliance / Scope Boundary Story - what the candidate implemented, what they only influenced, and what they did not own, while avoiding over-claiming. Teach how to convert real project experience into STAR format for each scenario. After the live explanation, the trainer hands the scenario documents to the candidate, who prepares from them and records one video per scenario (five video deliverables). Candidate maps their real project experience to each of the five scenarios.

Candidate creates and tests their own interview practice prompts.

Teach prompts for persona-specific questions
Teach prompts for JD-based practice
Teach prompts for follow-up questions

No retakes unless technical issue; submit before Day 5
Confirm scope and deadline
sections.candidate_focus: Confirm scope and deadline.

5.title: System Design Execution and Final Architecture Deliverable
5.day_objective: Prepare the candidate to explain a system design problem clearly using structured thinking, architecture flow, trade-offs, scalability, and diagram support.

focus_areas.objective: Teach a step-by-step system design interview flow.
Train candidate to ask clarifying questions before designing.
Candidate should explain components, data flow, APIs, storage, and services.
Candidate should justify choices and identify bottlenecks.
Candidate should use an image/diagram to support the explanation.

system_design_framework.requirement: Identify non-functional requirements: scale, latency, reliability, security.
Define core entities and data models.
Address scalability, bottlenecks, monitoring, and failure handling.

sections.name: Day 4 Review
sections.detail: Trainer reviews the Day 4 Resume-Based PUD 15-question deliverable and identifies the final gaps before moving into system design. Confirm resume ownership, PUD connection, persona-appropriate depth, and honest JD alignment, and give the last corrections the candidate should carry into their final deliverables.
key_points: Review the Day 4 resume-based PUD deliverable
Confirm resume ownership and PUD connection
Confirm persona-appropriate depth and honest JD alignment
Identify final gaps and corrections before system design
sections.candidate_focus: Understand corrections before system design.

sections.name: System Design Framework
sections.detail: Trainer teaches the step-by-step system design interview flow the candidate must follow. Walk the full ten-step framework: (1) clarify the problem statement; (2) identify functional requirements; (3) identify non-functional requirements such as scale, latency, reliability, and security; (4) define core entities and data models; (5) outline APIs and contracts; (6) draw the high-level architecture; (7) explain the end-to-end request flow; (8) deep-dive into one component; (9) explain trade-offs; and (10) address scalability, bottlenecks, monitoring, and failure handling. Stress asking clarifying questions before designing and structuring the answer before jumping to a solution.
key_points: Teach the full step-by-step system design flow
Step 1: clarify the problem statement
Step 2: identify functional requirements
Step 3: identify non-functional requirements (scale, latency, reliability, security)
Step 4: define core entities and data models
Step 5: outline APIs and contracts
Step 6: draw high-level architecture
Step 7: explain end-to-end request flow
Step 8: deep dive into one component
Step 9: explain trade-offs
Step 10: scalability, bottlenecks, monitoring, failure handling
Ask clarifying questions before designing
sections.candidate_focus: Understand the structure before attempting design.

sections.name: System Design Problem Walkthrough
sections.detail: Trainer works through one concrete system design problem end to end, applying the ten-step framework live so the candidate sees the structure in action - clarifying the problem, listing functional and non-functional requirements, defining entities and APIs, drawing architecture, explaining the request flow, deep-diving a component, and discussing trade-offs and scale. Candidate follows the structure and practices asking clarifying questions before solving.
key_points: Walk one system design problem step-by-step using the framework
Clarify problem -> requirements -> entities -> APIs -> architecture -> flow -> deep dive -> trade-offs -> scale
Model asking clarifying questions before solving
Candidate follows the structure and asks clarifying questions
sections.candidate_focus: Follow the structure and ask clarifying questions.

sections.name: Architecture Diagram Explanation
sections.detail: Trainer shows how to create a clean architecture diagram/image that supports the spoken explanation, with clear components and the flow between them, without over-designing. Cover what to include and what to leave out so the diagram aids understanding rather than cluttering it, and how the diagram should stay aligned with the walkthrough. This supports the System Design Image/Diagram deliverable, which must be clear, readable, and aligned with the walkthrough.
key_points: Show how to build a clean design diagram/image
Include clear components and the flow between them
Avoid over-designing / clutter
Keep the diagram aligned with the spoken walkthrough
Support the System Design Image/Diagram deliverable (clear, readable, aligned)
sections.candidate_focus: Understand how to use diagrams without over-designing.

sections.name: Trade-Offs, Bottlenecks and Defense
sections.detail: Trainer teaches how to reason about and defend design decisions. Cover scalability, reliability, caching, queues, databases, monitoring, and the failure points of a design, and how to justify why one option was chosen over the alternatives. Candidate practices defending a single design decision, identifying bottlenecks, and explaining scale considerations.
key_points: Explain scalability and reliability
Explain caching, queues, and databases
Explain monitoring and failure points
Justify design choices vs alternatives
Identify bottlenecks and scale considerations
Candidate practices defending one design decision
sections.candidate_focus: Practice defending one design decision.

sections.name: Final Deliverable Briefing
sections.detail: Trainer briefs the two final Day 5 deliverables and their quality bar. The deliverables are the System Design Problem Walkthrough (video, recommended 10-15 minutes) and the System Design Image/Diagram (a clear architecture diagram aligned with the walkthrough). State the rules: single continuous recording, no notes/prompts, no retakes unless a technical issue, the diagram/image must be clear, readable, and aligned with the explanation, and final submission after the Day 5 session.
key_points: Brief the two final Day 5 deliverables
System Design Problem Walkthrough video (10-15 min)
System Design Image/Diagram (clear, readable, aligned with walkthrough)
Single continuous recording; no notes/prompts; no retakes unless technical issue
Diagram must be clear, readable, and aligned with the explanation
Final submission after the Day 5 session
sections.candidate_focus: Confirm final Day 5 submissions.

homework.expected_output: Practice one full design problem using the framework.
Create a clean architecture image/diagram.
Practice design flow, trade-offs, and scalability aloud.
Review recording rules and ensure diagram clarity.

deliverables.scope: Clear architecture diagram aligned with walkthrough.

recording_submission_rules.requirement: Not allowed unless trainer requests due to technical issue.

evaluation_focus.requirement: Candidate clarifies and structures the problem before solving.
Candidate explains components and request flow clearly.
Diagram supports the answer and is not overly complex.
Candidate justifies design decisions.

exit_gate.pass: System design walkthrough and diagram submitted with quality bar met.
exit_gate.partial: Deliverables submitted but diagram, flow, or trade-off explanation needs correction.
exit_gate.hold: Missing deliverable, unclear diagram, no trade-offs, or unstructured explanation.
